note: Nomination-day report for the sixteen divisions of Hillsborough rural district, one member each. Eight divisions received a single nomination and are listed here; in Ballymacbrennan, Ballyskeagh, Breda, Carryduff, Drumbo, Edenderry and Ougley no nomination was made and the retiring members were deemed re-elected; five of them are recorded from Lisburn Standard reports of the council's meetings in August-November 1930 (meetings pass, 7 Nov 2026). The Lisburn Standard's nominations report (2 May 1930, p. 5) adds Blaris to the divisions with no nomination; Blaris (Samuel Brown) and Breda (James Dick, co-opted for Breda in 1927) are recorded from the August 1930 meeting (round 2, 7 Nov 2026). Ballyskeagh remains unnamed: its retiring member Robert Simpson was not seen at the meetings and was replaced by co-option in March 1931. Filed on Friday 30 May 1930, the day appointed by Down County Council for the county and rural district elections (Banbridge Chronicle, 15 March 1930, p. 2); previously filed under 1930-06-05 (provisional) (gap-fill 6 Nov 2026). Sole nomination; returned unopposed. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Renamed from 'Glassdrummond' to Glasdrumman (19 Nov 2026, w19-merges, the owner's decision 4 of 19 Nov 2026: a division filed under two spellings takes its official DED name, and each round keeps the spelling it was filed under as Constituency_Name_As_Printed): the 1911 DED map (Hillsborough Rural District) and the NI DED maps of 1921-39 name the DED Glasdrumman; the rounds were filed as Glassdrumman (1924, 1949-64) and Glassdrummond (1927-46, 1967). This round was filed as 'Glassdrummond', the spelling of its source, kept as Constituency_Name_As_Printed; the old address (glassdrummond) answers with a redirect to this one.
